topics.label: Lecture opening and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's themes and outlines the learning outcomes for cancer cell genetics and transformation.

topics.label: Tumor viruses, cellular oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the historical investigation of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established experimental methods for assaying malignant cell transformation.

topics.label: Classifications and functional mechanisms of cancer gene mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major categories of cancer-associated mutations and examine how alterations in genes like RB and p53 drive or restrain neoplastic growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the distinction between sequence and chromosomal instability, detailing how defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitotic segregation generate genomic abnormalities in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multistep tumor progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the stepwise accumulation of somatic mutations during tumorigenesis and examine how inherited genetic defects influence cancer susceptibility and tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, answers questions, and suggests additional reading.
